_: At the time of WWII, modern-day India was part of UK-controlled British India.
Declared war on Japan on Dec 8, 1941, the day after the Pearl Harbor attack. Germany and Italy declared war on Japan on Dec 11, 1941, prompting the US to respond in kind within hours.
At the time of WWII, modern-day Pakistan was part of UK-controlled British India.
At the time of WWII, modern-day Bangladesh was part of UK-controlled British India.
As Vietnam was occupied and ruled by Japan starting in 1940, Vietnam's allegiance was declared by the Viet Minh, who at the time were revolutionaries fighting to overthrow their Japanese occupiers.
Iran planned to remain neutral in WWII, but was occupied by both sides and eventually joined the Allies.
Maintained neutrality until they entered a friendship agreement with Germany in 1941, but did not send troops and declared war on Germany in 1945.

Originally one of the major Axis powers, Italy left the Axis once its dictatorial ruler, Benito Mussolini, was removed. Although Italy did not join the Allies, it did declare war on Germany, making it a co-belligerent which fought alongside the Allies.
South Korea's government was provisional at the time of its declaration.
Neutral government overthrown by coup in 1941. New regime supported Axis and fought against Britain, but was overthrown by Britain. Original government restored and supported the Allies.
Argentina remained neutral for most of the war. Did not sign the Declaration of United Nations, but did declare war on Germany.
Neutral through most of the war, but supported Allies with oil, hosted an Allied air base, and declared war on Germany and Japan in 1945.
Originally an Axis power, Romania surrendered to Russia in 1944 and subsequently became an Allied participant.
Bulgaria was part of the Axis powers from 1941-1944, then switched sides to the Allies in 1944.
